content:
Rina Kobayashi: posting a quick post-benchmark summary from last night’s mixed-workload runs (baseline vs scheduler flag ON). Full tables/plots are in the sheet but here’s the excerpt + what I think we should tune next.

Rina Kobayashi: Setup:
- Model: llama-3.1-70b-instruct (tp=4), runtime-1.19 build w/ `mixed_workload_scheduler=true`
- HW: H100 80GB (single node), driver 550.x, same kernel config across runs
- Load: 3 scenarios: synthetic mix (80/20), synthetic mix (50/50), + 1 trace replay ("cust-ish", anonymized)
- Metrics: TTFT p95/p99, E2E p95, throughput tok/s, queue wait split short/long

Rina Kobayashi: Excerpt (TTFT + throughput):
```text
Scenario                Baseline TTFT p95   Flag ON TTFT p95    Δ p95     Baseline TTFT p99   Flag ON TTFT p99   Δ p99     Baseline tok/s   Flag ON tok/s   Δ tok/s
---------------------   -----------------   -----------------   ------    -----------------   ----------------   ------    -------------    -----------    ------
Synth 80/20 (S/L)       420 ms              255 ms              -39%      980 ms              610 ms            -38%      18.7k            18.2k          -2.7%
Synth 50/50 (S/L)       610 ms              340 ms              -44%      1.42 s              0.91 s            -36%      17.9k            16.9k          -5.6%
Trace replay (cust-ish) 510 ms              310 ms              -39%      1.10 s              0.74 s            -33%      18.1k            17.6k          -2.8%

Long class E2E p95 (prefill-heavy): +6–9% across scenarios (mostly queueing). No starvation seen in these runs.
```

Rina Kobayashi: The “good news”: the main goal (short/interactive p95) is clearly moving in the right direction across all 3. TTFT p99 also improves materially.

Rina Kobayashi: The “needs work”: we’re paying a small throughput tax in the higher-mix case (50/50), and long-class E2E p95 is creeping up (not crazy, but it’s consistent).

Jonas Weber: this is great. Do you have the queueing breakdowns too? trying to see if we’re just shifting wait time from short->long or if there’s additional overhead.

Rina Kobayashi: yep. in 50/50, short queue wait p95 drops ~45% (as expected) but long queue wait p95 grows ~18%. Service time stays basically flat (within noise), so it looks like policy, not kernel.

Omar El-Sayed: +1 on “looks like policy”. I checked GPU util: baseline 91–92%, flag on 89–91% in 50/50. Might be a batching interaction or dispatch overhead.

Marcus Reed: do we know if this is before/after the lock contention fixes? I’m wondering if per-class queues increased lock hold time.

Rina Kobayashi: these runs are after PR 8444 (metrics) + 8439 (starvation guardrails) but *before* 8495 (lock contention optimizations). I can re-run after 8495 lands in the perf build.

Julian Moore: re metrics: I saw a couple spans in the trace where we were doing extra “peek” cycles (short empty, long not eligible yet due to fairness window). Might be contributing to the util dip.

Lena Fischer: can you paste what fairness window + weights were set to for these? want to sanity check.

Rina Kobayashi: config was the default from Marcus’ last commit:
- `short_queue_weight=1.0`
- `long_queue_min_share=0.15` (i.e., guarantee long gets 15% service over time)
- `max_short_burst_ms=12ms` (then we force a long dequeue if any pending)
- `classifier_prompt_len_threshold=1200 tokens` (plus the prefill cost stub)

Sofia Ivanova: thanks Rina. This is directionally what we wanted.
Question: in the trace replay, did we see any “priority inversion” signatures (short blocked behind a long prefill batch)?

Rina Kobayashi: not in this build. I think the inversion regression got addressed in PR 8468, but note: the trace run is from a newer build than the synthetic runs (sorry, I should’ve called that out). Synthetic was build 1.19.0-rc3, trace replay was 1.19.0-rc4 with 8468 cherry-picked.

Grace Kim: if 8468 is in rc4, that might also explain why trace replay looks “cleaner” than 50/50 synthetic.

Samir Qureshi: do we have any burst tests included? sometimes these policies oscillate under on/off arrival.

Rina Kobayashi: not yet in this batch. I only ran steady-state (after warmup) + one step-load at the end. Step-load looked stable but not enough to claim anything.

Jonas Weber: can we outline the next tuning steps so we can queue up another run batch?

Rina Kobayashi: proposed next steps (in order):
1) Re-run the full suite after 8495 (lock contention) to see if the tok/s dip in 50/50 is just scheduler overhead.
2) Sweep `max_short_burst_ms` (12ms -> 8ms/16ms) and `long_queue_min_share` (0.15 -> 0.10/0.20) and look at: short p95 vs long p95 and throughput.
3) Validate classifier sensitivity: threshold 1200 is probably too blunt. We should test 800/1200/1600 + enable the EWMA prefill estimate once PR 8480 is in.
4) Add one burst scenario (sine-ish or on/off) and confirm we don’t get queue oscillations / backlog growth.
5) If long p95 keeps creeping, consider admission control split (PR 8462) so long doesn’t inflate short during overload *and* we can cap long backlog growth.

Rina Kobayashi: I’ll kick off (1) tonight once perf build has 8495. If someone can put together suggested sweep ranges for (2)/(3), I’ll incorporate.

Marcus Reed: for (2), I’d rather sweep in “service quanta” terms, not ms. But we can approximate ms as long as the batch sizes are comparable.

Lena Fischer: agree. maybe express as “max N consecutive short dequeues” instead? less hardware dependent.

Sofia Ivanova: we can do both: keep ms for now (faster) but add a follow-up ticket to convert to token- or dequeue-count-based fairness later.

Omar El-Sayed: also note for dashboards: if we change these knobs, please keep metric names stable. I don’t want a repeat of last week’s bikeshed :)

Julian Moore: :thumbsup: I’ll ping on the metrics side once we confirm which queue wait histograms we’re keeping.

Rina Kobayashi: cool. linking the sheet + run IDs here:
- Results sheet (internal): https://drive.google.com/…/mixed-workload-benchmark-results
- Run IDs: H100-mixed-241114a (synth 80/20), H100-mixed-241114b (synth 50/50), H100-trace-241114c (trace)

Jonas Weber: thanks. once you have the 8495 rerun, drop the same excerpt format here so we can make a go/no-go call for perf-canary.

Sofia Ivanova: +1. if throughput dip stays <= ~3% and we keep the short p95 win, I’m comfortable moving to perf-canary with default-off.

Rina Kobayashi: ack. I’ll post an update in-thread after the reruns.
